I used to have a copy of "Lincos: Design of a Language for Cosmic Intercourse", by Hans Freudenthal, 1960[1].

The book is literally a series of messages you can transmit by radio to an alien intelligence somewhere else in the universe so you can establish a language in common with them. It starts off by teaching numbers: ., .., ..., i.e., sending 1 pulse, 2 pulses, 3 pulses, and so on, teaches numbers to an extraterrestrial being. From this it creates arithmetic (".. pause ... longer-pause .....", means 2+3=5), and then creates abbreviations for symbols, and goes on the build up a lot of mathematics, and then the concept of time, and basic physics, and even very abstract ideas like "good" and "bad", though I've forgotten how it managed to encode that (but I recall it seemed plausible at the time I read the book).

The book is impossible to find now. I'd love to get a PDF version of it.

A separate question. Consider I'm responding here to (amongst other things):

> And I think all those vibe-coded software will not stand the test of time.

When I use LLMs to write software for me, it is rare that I think "this is great, I should share it". Even when I do, I am aware of how fast these things are improving, so while I put great effort into, for example, having Claude make me a nice isochrone map generator, I fully expect that a year from now any similar project (even if different enough the LLM will not simply clone my git repo) will be a one-shot prompt.

What I did will only stand the test of time if all the AI labs shut down and nobody takes over from them. Same with vibe-Photoshop-clones: a year from now, anyone who wants this kind of thing will get it with one prompt, not thousands, and this specific instance will likely be forgotten.
